name: LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse
purpose: Meituan states: a non-thinking MoE built on LongCat-Flash-Lite that replaces dense MLA with LongCat Sparse Attention (LSA) to support 1 M tokens of context and to improve agentic coding, search and tool use.

lineage.how_derived: dense MLA replaced by LSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention extended with streaming-aware, cross-layer and hierarchical indexing), long-context extension to 1,024K

license.name: MIT
license.notes: LICENSE file read: standard MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Meituan; the card states weights and source code are MIT.

architecture.gguf_arch: none in mainline llama.cpp (community fork only)
architecture.attention: LongCat Sparse Attention (LSA): streaming-aware indexing (sink and local window plus dynamic selection), cross-layer index reuse, optional hierarchical indexing at inference
architecture.drafter: native MTP (preserved in a community GGUF; official repo does not describe it)
architecture.why_this_design: Meituan states: LSA turns fragmented KV access into contiguous reads, improving HBM efficiency; cross-layer reuse exploits stable attention saliency; hierarchical indexing lowers indexing overhead and needs no extra training.

variants.format: GGUF Q3_K_M (uncensored derivative, needs a llama.cpp fork)
variants.notes: refusal-removed derivative, not the vendor model; behaviour differs

engine_support.notes: Mainline llama.cpp lacks the LongCat-Flash-Lite arch (PR 19167 in progress as of 2026-08-06) and has no LSA; the community GGUFs need a fork. Tona would need a new module (LSA indexer, 256 experts).

strengths: 3 B active: cheap decode; non-thinking: short answers and low latency
Large gain over the dense Lite on SWE-bench Verified (54.4 to 68.2) and Multilingual (38.1 to 59.3)
weaknesses: Vendor SWE-bench Verified 68.2 against 79.2 to 82.8 for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next family and 79 for Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B
No official GGUF and no mainline llama.cpp support
best_for: low-latency coding help where a thinking model is too slow, once an engine supports LSA
avoid_for: today: anything that needs a stock llama.cpp
soft.maturity: Meituan LongCat: three releases in 2026; 1.2k downloads of this repo, 3 discussions.

user_reports.summary: Community asks for GGUF; mainline llama.cpp does not support the base arch, a fork author says Sparse needs "a lot of extra work"

tona_fit.reason: MIT (verified) and a size that fits 16 GB + 64 GB at Q3/Q4 (33 to 41 GB), but its vendor agent numbers are below the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Ornith class and nothing independent exists. Candidate only if a coding-calibrated quant or an independent score changes that.
blockers: Tona has no LSA module (engine support, not a quality judgement)
